purpose: Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Named after the MUI Transfer List (Ant Design calls it Transfer; it was PickList before 6.0), written to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<TransferList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, `<TransferList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<TransferList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.
useWhen: Use TransferList only when the person builds a large subset and must see the chosen and remaining items side by side. To pick several values in a compact form field use MultiSelect; for two to five options use a Checkbox per option.
Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.
avoidWhen: Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
related: `multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
bestPractices: Set `item-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves and the selection follows the record when the lists change; without it rows and the selection are keyed by their index.
Set `title` on both `TransferList.Source` and `TransferList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.
